items.item: Facebook's monitoring systems generated more than two billion unique time series of counters, with about twelve million data points added per second, as of spring 2015.

items.item: A cloud-only pipeline that treats the WAN link as always available blanks every plant's dashboard on the first real outage.

at.step: Hook: a WAN outage blanks the plants, then floods them

items.item: The edge buffer's own size is a straight multiplication: an outage's length times the rate it has to hold.

at.step: Reveal: the edge gateway's buffer, sized from the outage

items.item: A durable log decouples every plant from every consumer regardless of which delivery level a given signal class is held to.

at.step: Reveal: the protocol boundary and the delivery level

items.item: Joining the asset context early costs storage on every event; joining it late costs a lookup on every query.

at.step: Reveal: two stores, a cardinality limit, and where the asset joins in

items.item: Plant-local autonomy during an outage is a degraded mode with its own recovery target per signal class, not an afterthought.

at.step: Reveal: plant-local autonomy, and residency per site

items.item: A catch-up with no throttle just moves the outage's own damage from the outage to the moment the link returns.

at.step: Reveal: the throttled, idempotent catch-up

items.item: At ten times the sensor count, the next bottleneck is the hot store's own cardinality, not the WAN link.

at.step: Prove it: ten times the sensors

items.item: This topic leaves out the industrial data model, OPC UA, MQTT, Sparkplug, historians, time-series storage engines, and edge buffering as later-chapter forward pointers.
Store-and-forward edge buffering, per-signal delivery levels, and throttled idempotent catch-up are each established practice, not an emerging technique.
A platform that collects the readings is half the system; the other half decides, as they arrive, whether a line is drifting out of spec.
